name: Modmail
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Modmail is a Discord bot that turns members' direct messages into threads your staff answer together. It needs a Discord bot token and a MongoDB database, such as a free MongoDB Atlas one.
startup: export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 DISABLE_AUTOUPDATES=true DISABLE_UPDATES=true; h=$( (python3 --version; cat requirements.txt) | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1); if [ "$h" != "$(cat .venv/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing Modmail's dependencies"; rm -rf .venv; { python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt && echo "$h" > .venv/.raptor-installed; } || exit 1; fi; for v in TOKEN CONNECTION_URI GUILD_ID OWNERS LOG_URL; do [ -n "${!v}" ] || unset $v; done; need=; for v in TOKEN CONNECTION_URI GUILD_ID OWNERS; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || grep -qE "^$v=.+" .env 2>/dev/null || need=1; done; if [ -n "$need" ]; then if .venv/bin/python -c "import discord, motor, cairosvg, lottie" 2>/dev/null; then echo "Modmail is installed, but needs a Discord bot token, a MongoDB connection string, a server ID and owner IDs: set them in Startup, then restart the server."; exec sleep infinity; else echo "Modmail's dependencies are broken. Restart the server to install them again."; rm -f .venv/.raptor-installed; exit 1; fi; fi; exec .venv/bin/python bot.py

config.startup: {"done": ["regex:Logged in as: ", "regex:^Modmail is installed, but needs"]}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Modmail: downloads the chosen release's source from GitHub. .env,
# installed plugins and everything else of the owner's are kept; its
# Python dependencies are installed when the server starts, for the Python
# it runs on. Its settings and threads live in the owner's MongoDB.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
tag=latest
if [ "$want" != latest ]; then tag="v${want#v}"; fi
tag=$(gh-release tag modmail-dev/Modmail "$tag") || fail "There's no Modmail release $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 4.2.1, then reinstall."
version="${tag#v}"

if [ -f bot.py ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-modmail 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Modmail $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Modmail $version"
    curl -fsSL -o "$work/modmail.tar.gz" "https://github.com/modmail-dev/Modmail/archive/refs/tags/$tag.tar.gz" || fail "Modmail $version couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$work/new"
    tar -xzf "$work/modmail.tar.gz" -C "$work/new" --strip-components=1
    [ -f "$work/new/bot.py" ] && [ -f "$work/new/requirements.txt" ] || fail "The Modmail $version download isn't a Modmail release."
    rm -rf "$work/new/.github" "$work/new/Dockerfile" "$work/new/docker-compose.yml" "$work/new/.dockerignore" "$work/new/app.json" "$work/new/Procfile"
    # The program: files from the last release that this one dropped go,
    # the rest are replaced. Plugins the owner installed stay; the plugin
    # registry comes from the release.
    if [ -f .raptor-files ]; then
        while IFS= read -r e; do
            if [ -n "$e" ] && [ "$e" != plugins ] && [ ! -e "$work/new/$e" ]; then rm -rf -- "./$e"; fi
        done < .raptor-files
    fi
    find "$work/new" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name plugins -printf '%f\n' > "$work/files"
    while IFS= read -r e; do
        rm -rf -- "./$e"
        mv "$work/new/$e" "./$e"
    done < "$work/files"
    echo plugins >> "$work/files"
    mkdir -p plugins
    cp -Rn "$work/new/plugins/." plugins/
    cp -f "$work/new/plugins/registry.json" plugins/
    mv -f "$work/files" .raptor-files
    echo "$tag" > .raptor-modmail
fi
echo "Installed Modmail $version."

variables.name: Discord bot token
variables.description: The bot's token, from the Discord Developer Portal, with the server members and message content intents on.

variables.name: MongoDB connection string
variables.description: Where Modmail keeps its settings and threads, such as mongodb+srv://user:password@cluster.mongodb.net.

variables.name: Server ID
variables.description: The ID of the Discord server members message the bot from.

variables.name: Owner IDs
variables.description: The Discord user IDs of the bot's owners, separated by commas.

variables.name: Log viewer address
variables.description: The address of your Modmail log viewer, if you run one, for links to closed threads.

variables.name: Send usage data
variables.description: Send anonymous usage data (server and member counts) to Modmail's developers once an hour.

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Modmail version to install, such as 4.2.1, or latest. Reinstall to change it.
